title: Fish fries, home brew, lawn parties and tarpaulin dancing
summary: Friday fish fries, backyard home brew, social clubs' dances, and dancing on rented tarpaulins in lawn parties.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Especially, you know, if you knew who was cooking it and you know they know how to cook. Yeah. So in them days, like I think I told you before, them people on a Friday, very few people in certain neighborhoods would cook. They'd say, well so and so got a fish Friday night. We'd get some gumbo, potato salad, some fish and potato salad for supper, you know. People would have that furnace in the yard, see. That's where they'd hang out the red light brush. They'd hang out the district night. They'd hang out the red light and out the gate. See out the side of the gate, somebody would have a stick, you know, stick and wear out the gate. They'd say, oh you've got a fish fry with that night, let's go over here and give her a play or give this to play. Well they'd have that home brew in the backyard you know. And you want a home brew? Well you'd go in the backyard and drink the home brew. You wouldn't be out there in the front, you know. Everything else was at. Things was dry. Was there any certain nights for lawn parties Q or? I think lawn parties was on a Sunday or Sunday night. A lawn, just give a lot of lawn parties. I've gone to a couple of them on Sunday night.
And then ten years ago or something.

Yeah, because of what, twenty years, twenty-five years ago. I played for a lot of them. They used to have a lot of clubs here. You know youngsters, instead of running around the street looking for something to drink, they'd have clubs where they'd have meetings a couple of times a week and then every so of them they'd give a dance and hire a band. Because I remember one club in particular I used to like to play, it was called the Cornation Club downtown. But I mean every ward had maybe one or two clubs you know, and they'd play cards or play bingo for entertainment. And the other things were just so much different you know than it is nowadays.
Well when they lawn parties, did they dance something along?

Yeah. Well some places if they had a rough yard they used to rent a tapoian. And they put a tapoian in the yard and they danced on a tapoian. Some people had nice smooth yards, well they danced on the mud. Or some people's yards in the pav, they danced on the pav. But the majority of people had mud yards, well they'd rent a tapoian and they danced on a tapoian.
Yeah, but that seemed like it'd be a little rough or sticky to slide around your feet on that too.

Well I don't know, but they used to dance on it because my dad used to rent a tapoian and they used to put a tapoian in the people, well they'd be responsible for it and nobody wouldn't smoke and drop cigarette butts on it or whatnot you see. But that's what they used to do, spread that big tapoian in the yard and the band sitting on the side and everybody had a lovely time. Very something they had to fight or anything like that. Yeah. Now you go to some of these dances, you have to bring a cannon with you. Yeah. Yeah. Because the harmony and the cast of their band for the weekend, you know, because this thing going on, say the teenagers might come break up the place.
